I can't rule out to (2,4,1), to (1,2,2), to (1,4,4) or to (1,6,2) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (2,4,1).
Going to (2,2,1) would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (4,4,1).
The line must go to (6,4,1): to (4,2,1) is number 13, which comes later; to (4,6,1) is number 22, which comes later.
Going to (6,2,1) would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going to (6,6,1), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes to (7,4,2).
Going to (7,4,4) would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (7,6,2).
Going to (6,7,2) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (6,6,1).
The line must go to (6,7,2): to (4,6,1) is number 22, which comes later.
Going to (4,7,2) would force the line onto number 22 before its turn. So the line goes to (6,7,4).
Number 4 is only reachable this way.
Going to (7,6,6) would force the line onto number 6 before its turn; going to (6,6,7), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,6,7). So the line goes to (4,7,6).
Going to (2,7,6) would leave number 6 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going to (4,7,4) would leave number 6 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (4,6,7).
The line must go to (6,6,7): to (2,6,7) is number 23, which comes later; to (4,4,7) is number 16, which comes later.
Going to (6,4,7) would leave number 6 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (7,6,6).
Number 6 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going to (7,2,6), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 8. So the line goes to (6,4,7).
Number 8 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going to (4,2,7) would force the line onto number 16 before its turn; going to (7,2,6), the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,1,4). So the line goes to (6,1,6).
Cell (7,2,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (7,2,4).
Going to (4,1,4), the next 7 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,2,2). So the line goes to (6,1,2).
Going to (4,1,2) would strand number 12: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going to (6,2,1) would turn number 12 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes to (7,2,2).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (6,2,1).
Going to (4,1,2) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (2,2,1).
Going to number 14 would leave both cell (1,2,2) and cell (4,1,2) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (1,2,2).
Number 14 is only reachable this way.
The line must go to (4,1,2): to (2,1,4) is number 19, which comes later.
Going to (2,1,6) would force the line onto number 19 before its turn. So the line goes to (4,2,7).
Going to (2,2,7) would strand number 16: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (4,4,7).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,4,7).
Number 17 is only reachable this way.
Going to (1,4,4) would cut off a group of 5 cells; going to (1,6,6) would leave number 18 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (1,2,6).
Cell (2,2,7) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,1,6).
Going to (2,7,4) would cut off a group of 3 cells; going to (1,6,6) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (1,6,2).
Going to number 21, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 22. So the line goes to (2,7,2).

Going to (2,7,4) would strand number 21: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going to (4,7,2) would leave both cell (4,7,4) and number 22 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (2,6,1).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,6,1).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
